text: What was the total value in EUR of all transactions with status CAPTURED whose ts_utc falls on 2025-03-14 UTC (2025-03-14 00:00:00 <= ts_utc < 2025-03-15 00:00:00)? Convert every transaction amount to EUR (major units) using the daily FX rate (EUR per unit of the transaction currency) for the transaction date. Answer with one number in EUR rounded to 2 decimals, e.g. 12345.67.
gt_sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(t.amount_minor / power(10, c.exponent) * f.rate_to_eur), 2) AS eur_total
FROM txn t
JOIN dim_currency c ON c.currency_id = t.currency_id
JOIN fx_rate f ON f.currency_id = t.currency_id AND f.rate_date = substr(t.ts_utc, 1, 10)
JOIN txn_status_dict s ON s.status_id = t.status_id
WHERE s.code = 'CAPTURED'
  AND t.ts_utc >= '2025-03-14 00:00:00' AND t.ts_utc < '2025-03-15 00:00:00'
rationale: amount_minor must be scaled by 10^exponent per currency (JPY=0, KWD=3) before applying the daily rate; dividing everything by 100 inflates JPY and deflates KWD amounts.

text: Consider all transactions (any status) made on terminals that were assigned, at the time of each transaction, to a merchant belonging to merchant group 'Helios Grocery' or to any of its sub-groups (at any depth). Which ISO-8601 week had the largest number of such transactions in 2025? Answer in the format YYYY-Www, e.g. 2025-W07.
gt_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE grp(group_id) AS (
  SELECT group_id FROM dim_merchant_group WHERE name = 'Helios Grocery'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT g.group_id FROM dim_merchant_group g JOIN grp ON g.parent_group_id = grp.group_id
)
SELECT strftime('%Y', date(t.ts_utc, '-' || ((strftime('%w', t.ts_utc) + 6) % 7) || ' days', '+3 days')) || '-W' || printf('%02d', (strftime('%j', date(t.ts_utc, '-' || ((strftime('%w', t.ts_utc) + 6) % 7) || ' days', '+3 days')) - 1) / 7 + 1) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM txn t
JOIN terminal_assignment ta ON ta.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
  AND t.ts_utc >= ta.valid_from AND (ta.valid_to IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < ta.valid_to)
JOIN dim_merchant m ON m.merchant_id = ta.merchant_id
JOIN grp ON grp.group_id = m.group_id
GROUP BY iso_week ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1
rationale: The group is a level-2 division; its merchants hang off level-3 chains, so a recursive roll-up is needed. SQLite's %W is not the ISO week (off by one in 2025); growth + December bump put the peak in W51.

text: What was the total value in EUR of CAPTURED transactions in the first half of 2025 (2025-01-01 00:00:00 <= ts_utc < 2025-07-01 00:00:00) made on terminals that were assigned, at the time of the transaction, to merchants of merchant group 'Aurora Hospitality' or any of its sub-groups? Convert amounts to EUR with the daily FX rate of the transaction date. Answer with one number in EUR rounded to 2 decimals.
gt_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE grp(group_id) AS (
  SELECT group_id FROM dim_merchant_group WHERE name = 'Aurora Hospitality'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT g.group_id FROM dim_merchant_group g JOIN grp ON g.parent_group_id = grp.group_id
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(t.amount_minor / power(10, c.exponent) * f.rate_to_eur), 2) AS eur_total
FROM txn t
JOIN terminal_assignment ta ON ta.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
  AND t.ts_utc >= ta.valid_from AND (ta.valid_to IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < ta.valid_to)
JOIN dim_merchant m ON m.merchant_id = ta.merchant_id
JOIN grp ON grp.group_id = m.group_id
JOIN dim_currency c ON c.currency_id = t.currency_id
JOIN fx_rate f ON f.currency_id = t.currency_id AND f.rate_date = substr(t.ts_utc, 1, 10)
JOIN txn_status_dict s ON s.status_id = t.status_id
WHERE s.code = 'CAPTURED'
  AND t.ts_utc >= '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND t.ts_utc < '2025-07-01 00:00:00'
rationale: The 'Aurora Coffee Chain' (a sub-group) sold its 44 terminals on 2025-06-16; they now belong to merchants of another holding. Joining on the current assignment drops their H1 volume.

text: For terminal model 'P400', what was the decline rate in August 2025 (2025-08-01 00:00:00 <= ts_utc < 2025-09-01 00:00:00)? A transaction counts as declined if its response code is flagged as a decline in the response-code dictionary version that was valid at the transaction's timestamp. Decline rate = declined transactions / all transactions of that model in the month (any status). Answer as a decimal fraction rounded to 4 decimals, e.g. 0.0712.
gt_sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(rc.is_decline), 4) AS decline_rate
FROM txn t
JOIN dim_terminal d ON d.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
JOIN dim_terminal_model mo ON mo.model_id = d.model_id
JOIN response_code_dict rc ON rc.code = t.response_code
  AND t.ts_utc >= rc.valid_from AND (rc.valid_to IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < rc.valid_to)
WHERE mo.model_name = 'P400'
  AND t.ts_utc >= '2025-08-01 00:00:00' AND t.ts_utc < '2025-09-01 00:00:00'
rationale: Scheme version 2 (valid from 2025-07-01) re-classifies code 96 (decline -> timeout) and 68 (timeout -> decline); August must be classified with version 2. P400 belongs to the OSX-3 family, whose declines rose after the 2025-08-04 firmware rollout.

text: Among terminal firmware families with at least 10,000 transactions in Q4 2025 (2025-10-01 00:00:00 <= ts_utc < 2026-01-01 00:00:00), which family had the highest decline rate? A transaction is declined if its response code is flagged as a decline in the response-code dictionary version valid at the transaction time; decline rate = declined / all transactions of the family in Q4. Answer with the firmware family name exactly as stored.
gt_sql:
SELECT mo.firmware_family
FROM txn t
JOIN dim_terminal d ON d.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
JOIN dim_terminal_model mo ON mo.model_id = d.model_id
JOIN response_code_dict rc ON rc.code = t.response_code
  AND t.ts_utc >= rc.valid_from AND (rc.valid_to IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < rc.valid_to)
WHERE t.ts_utc >= '2025-10-01 00:00:00' AND t.ts_utc < '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY mo.firmware_family
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10000
ORDER BY AVG(rc.is_decline) DESC LIMIT 1
rationale: Firmware 3.7.2 of family OSX-3 (models V240m, P400) raised declines by ~4.5 pp from 2025-08-04; the other families stay at ~6.5 %.

text: Consider CAPTURED transactions attributed (through the terminal assignment valid at the time of the transaction) to merchants of merchant group 'Helios Grocery' or any of its sub-groups, converted to EUR with the daily FX rate of the transaction date. What was the first calendar month of 2025 in which their total EUR value exceeded 280,000 EUR? Answer in the format YYYY-MM.
gt_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE grp(group_id) AS (
  SELECT group_id FROM dim_merchant_group WHERE name = 'Helios Grocery'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT g.group_id FROM dim_merchant_group g JOIN grp ON g.parent_group_id = grp.group_id
)
SELECT month FROM (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', t.ts_utc) AS month, SUM(t.amount_minor / power(10, c.exponent) * f.rate_to_eur) AS eur
  FROM txn t
  JOIN terminal_assignment ta ON ta.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
  AND t.ts_utc >= ta.valid_from AND (ta.valid_to IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < ta.valid_to)
JOIN dim_merchant m ON m.merchant_id = ta.merchant_id
JOIN grp ON grp.group_id = m.group_id
  JOIN dim_currency c ON c.currency_id = t.currency_id
JOIN fx_rate f ON f.currency_id = t.currency_id AND f.rate_date = substr(t.ts_utc, 1, 10)
  JOIN txn_status_dict s ON s.status_id = t.status_id
  WHERE s.code = 'CAPTURED'
  GROUP BY month
)
WHERE eur > 280000
ORDER BY month LIMIT 1
rationale: The group grows ~70 % over the year; the threshold 280,000 EUR sits in the widest gap between a month and the maximum of all earlier months, so the answer is robust to rounding.

text: Incident INC-2025-0005 is linked to service events through correlation ids. Find the earliest ERROR-level service event linked to this incident. Which deployment of the incident's component was the most recent one deployed strictly before that event? Answer with the deployment's version string exactly as stored.
gt_sql:
WITH inc AS (SELECT incident_id, component_id FROM incident WHERE code = 'INC-2025-0005'),
first_err AS (
  SELECT MIN(e.ts_utc) AS ts
  FROM service_event e
  JOIN incident_link l ON l.correlation_id = e.correlation_id
  JOIN inc ON inc.incident_id = l.incident_id
  WHERE e.level = 'ERROR')
SELECT d.version
FROM deployment d JOIN inc ON inc.component_id = d.component_id
WHERE d.deployed_at < (SELECT ts FROM first_err)
ORDER BY d.deployed_at DESC LIMIT 1
rationale: First linked ERROR is at 2025-03-11 14:21:07; the last deployment before it is v4.18.0 (2025-03-11 14:05:00). A '+restart' re-deploy happened between the first error and the incident opening, and an unlinked ERROR occurred earlier that day.

text: Component 'auth-router' had a deployment with version 'v4.18.0'; let T be its deployed_at. For transactions on the route with code 'ALP-PRX-1', compute the average latency_ms over [T, T + 120 minutes) divided by the average latency_ms over [T - 120 minutes, T) (all transactions regardless of status). Answer with the ratio rounded to 2 decimals.
gt_sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT dp.deployed_at AS t0 FROM deployment dp
  JOIN dim_component c ON c.component_id = dp.component_id
  WHERE c.name = 'auth-router' AND dp.version = 'v4.18.0'),
r AS (SELECT route_id FROM route WHERE code = 'ALP-PRX-1')
SELECT ROUND(
  (SELECT AVG(t.latency_ms) FROM txn t, d, r WHERE t.route_id = r.route_id
     AND t.ts_utc >= d.t0 AND t.ts_utc < datetime(d.t0, '+120 minutes')) /
  (SELECT AVG(t.latency_ms) FROM txn t, d, r WHERE t.route_id = r.route_id
     AND t.ts_utc >= datetime(d.t0, '-120 minutes') AND t.ts_utc < d.t0), 2) AS ratio
rationale: The bad release multiplied latency x4 on that route and produced 'Z1' processor timeouts (8-30 s), so the mean latency after the deployment is an order of magnitude higher than before.

text: During incident INC-2025-0018 (from its opened_at inclusive to its closed_at exclusive), what share of transactions on the routes of acquirer 'Meridian Acquiring' ended in a timeout? A timeout is a response code flagged as timeout in the response-code dictionary version valid at the transaction time. Share = timeout transactions / all transactions on those routes in the window (any status). Answer as a decimal fraction rounded to 4 decimals.
gt_sql:
WITH inc AS (SELECT opened_at, closed_at FROM incident WHERE code = 'INC-2025-0018')
SELECT ROUND(AVG(rc.is_timeout), 4) AS timeout_share
FROM txn t
JOIN route r ON r.route_id = t.route_id
JOIN dim_acquirer a ON a.acquirer_id = r.acquirer_id
JOIN response_code_dict rc ON rc.code = t.response_code
  AND t.ts_utc >= rc.valid_from AND (rc.valid_to IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < rc.valid_to)
JOIN inc
WHERE a.name = 'Meridian Acquiring'
  AND t.ts_utc >= inc.opened_at AND t.ts_utc < inc.closed_at
rationale: During the outage the acquirer returned Z3/91/96; code 96 is a timeout only in scheme version 2 (valid in September), so classifying with version 1 under-counts timeouts.

text: Treat every deployment (deployed_at) and every config change (changed_at) as a 'change' made by its operator on a component. An incident is preceded by a change if the change is on the incident's component and 0 <= opened_at - change time <= 60 minutes. Which operator has the largest number of distinct incidents preceded by their changes? Answer with the operator's login.
gt_sql:
WITH changes AS (
  SELECT component_id, operator_id, deployed_at AS at FROM deployment
  UNION ALL
  SELECT component_id, operator_id, changed_at FROM config_change),
hits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ch.operator_id, i.incident_id
  FROM incident i
  JOIN changes ch ON ch.component_id = i.component_id
    AND ch.at <= i.opened_at AND ch.at >= datetime(i.opened_at, '-60 minutes'))
SELECT o.login
FROM hits h JOIN operator o ON o.operator_id = h.operator_id
GROUP BY o.login ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
rationale: r.svensson (SRE) made config changes 21-44 minutes before four different incidents; the runner-ups have 2 (d.kowalski: the bad auth-router release plus one more deployment; j.mueller: two 'mitigation' changes).

text: How many settlements were converted with an FX rate that deviates from the official daily rate? Count the settlements where |fx_rate_applied - R| / R > 0.005, where R is the official FX rate (EUR per unit of the transaction's currency) for the calendar date of settled_at (UTC). Answer with an integer.
gt_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n
FROM settlement s
JOIN txn t ON t.txn_id = s.txn_id
JOIN fx_rate f ON f.currency_id = t.currency_id AND f.rate_date = substr(s.settled_at, 1, 10)
WHERE ABS(s.fx_rate_applied - f.rate_to_eur) / f.rate_to_eur > 0.005
rationale: The fx-service cache TTL was set to 7 days on 2025-05-12 09:14:00; settlement batches 2025-05-13..2025-05-19 used the 2025-05-12 snapshot. Only non-EUR settlements whose rate had drifted > 0.5 % by then are counted.

text: Call a settlement 'mis-rated' if |fx_rate_applied - R| / R > 0.005, where R is the official FX rate (EUR per unit of the transaction's currency) for the calendar date of settled_at. Take the earliest mis-rated settlement by settled_at. Which config change on component 'fx-service' was the most recent one made strictly before that settlement time? Answer with its change_id (integer).
gt_sql:
WITH first_bad AS (
  SELECT MIN(s.settled_at) AS ts
  FROM settlement s
  JOIN txn t ON t.txn_id = s.txn_id
  JOIN fx_rate f ON f.currency_id = t.currency_id AND f.rate_date = substr(s.settled_at, 1, 10)
  WHERE ABS(s.fx_rate_applied - f.rate_to_eur) / f.rate_to_eur > 0.005)
SELECT cc.change_id
FROM config_change cc
JOIN dim_component c ON c.component_id = cc.component_id
WHERE c.name = 'fx-service' AND cc.changed_at < (SELECT ts FROM first_bad)
ORDER BY cc.changed_at DESC LIMIT 1
rationale: The first settlement with > 0.5 % deviation is in the 2025-05-14 batch; the last fx-service change before it is the rate_cache_ttl_seconds 300 -> 604800 change of 2025-05-12 09:14:00 (a later log.level decoy precedes the incident's opened_at instead).

text: Which top-level merchant group (a group without a parent group) had the highest total EUR value of CAPTURED transactions in November 2025 (2025-11-01 00:00:00 <= ts_utc < 2025-12-01 00:00:00)? Attribute each transaction to the merchant the terminal was assigned to at the time of the transaction, roll every merchant up through the whole group hierarchy to its top-level group, and convert amounts to EUR with the daily FX rate of the transaction date. Answer with the top-level group's name.
gt_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE tree(group_id, root_id) AS (
  SELECT group_id, group_id FROM dim_merchant_group WHERE parent_group_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT g.group_id, tree.root_id FROM dim_merchant_group g JOIN tree ON g.parent_group_id = tree.group_id)
SELECT rg.name
FROM txn t
JOIN terminal_assignment ta ON ta.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
  AND t.ts_utc >= ta.valid_from AND (ta.valid_to IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < ta.valid_to)
JOIN dim_merchant m ON m.merchant_id = ta.merchant_id
JOIN tree ON tree.group_id = m.group_id
JOIN dim_merchant_group rg ON rg.group_id = tree.root_id
JOIN dim_currency c ON c.currency_id = t.currency_id
JOIN fx_rate f ON f.currency_id = t.currency_id AND f.rate_date = substr(t.ts_utc, 1, 10)
JOIN txn_status_dict s ON s.status_id = t.status_id
WHERE s.code = 'CAPTURED'
  AND t.ts_utc >= '2025-11-01 00:00:00' AND t.ts_utc < '2025-12-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY rg.name ORDER BY SUM(t.amount_minor / power(10, c.exponent) * f.rate_to_eur) DESC LIMIT 1
rationale: Most merchants hang off level-3 chains; only one flagship store per holding is attached directly to the top-level group, so without the roll-up the ranking is driven by those few stores.

text: For terminals whose model belongs to firmware family 'OSX-3', what was the first calendar month of 2025 in which the monthly decline rate exceeded 9.0 %? A transaction is declined if its response code is flagged as a decline in the response-code dictionary version valid at the transaction time; monthly decline rate = declined / all transactions of these terminals in that month. Answer in the format YYYY-MM.
gt_sql:
SELECT month FROM (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', t.ts_utc) AS month, AVG(rc.is_decline) AS rate
  FROM txn t
  JOIN dim_terminal d ON d.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
JOIN dim_terminal_model mo ON mo.model_id = d.model_id
  JOIN response_code_dict rc ON rc.code = t.response_code
  AND t.ts_utc >= rc.valid_from AND (rc.valid_to IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < rc.valid_to)
  WHERE mo.firmware_family = 'OSX-3'
  GROUP BY month)
WHERE rate > 0.09
ORDER BY month LIMIT 1
rationale: Firmware 3.7.2 was pushed to the OSX-3 fleet on 2025-08-04 02:00 UTC; the family's decline rate jumps from ~6.5 % to ~10.5 % in August and stays there.

text: What was the total value in EUR of CAPTURED transactions in 2025 attributed to the top-level merchant group 'Aurora Collective' including all of its sub-groups at any depth? Attribute each transaction to the merchant the terminal was linked to at the time of the transaction, and convert amounts to EUR with the daily FX rate of the transaction date. Answer with one number in EUR rounded to 2 decimals.
gt_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE grp(group_id) AS (
  SELECT group_id FROM dim_merchant_group WHERE name = 'Aurora Collective'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT g.group_id FROM dim_merchant_group g JOIN grp ON g.parent_group_id = grp.group_id
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(t.amount_minor / power(10, c.exponent) * f.eur_per_unit), 2) AS eur_total
FROM txn t
JOIN terminal_merchant_link tl ON tl.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
  AND t.ts_utc >= tl.start_ts AND (tl.end_ts IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < tl.end_ts)
JOIN dim_merchant m ON m.merchant_id = tl.merchant_id
JOIN grp ON grp.group_id = m.merchant_group_id
JOIN dim_currency c ON c.currency_id = t.currency_id
JOIN fx_rate_daily f ON f.currency_id = t.currency_id AND f.rate_date = substr(t.ts_utc, 1, 10)
JOIN txn_status_dict s ON s.status_id = t.status_id
WHERE s.code = 'CAPTURED'
rationale: Same knowledge as q03/q13 under the renamed schema (terminal_merchant_link.start_ts/end_ts, dim_merchant.merchant_group_id, fx_rate_daily.eur_per_unit); the coffee chain's H1 volume belongs to Aurora only through the historical link.

text: Which ISO-8601 week of 2025 had the largest number of ERROR-level service events for component 'auth-router'? Consider all service events of the whole year 2025. Answer in the format YYYY-Www, e.g. 2025-W07.
gt_sql:
WITH ev AS (
  SELECT ts_utc, component_id, level FROM service_event_h1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ts_utc, component_id, level FROM service_event_h2)
SELECT strftime('%Y', date(e.ts_utc, '-' || ((strftime('%w', e.ts_utc) + 6) % 7) || ' days', '+3 days')) || '-W' || printf('%02d', (strftime('%j', date(e.ts_utc, '-' || ((strftime('%w', e.ts_utc) + 6) % 7) || ' days', '+3 days')) - 1) / 7 + 1) AS iso_week
FROM ev e JOIN dim_component c ON c.component_id = e.component_id
WHERE c.name = 'auth-router' AND e.level = 'ERROR'
GROUP BY iso_week ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
rationale: The log table is split into service_event_h1/h2; the March release incident (W11) has more ERRORs than the October capacity incident (W41), which is the maximum if only h2 is read.

text: For terminal model 'Lane 3000X', what was the decline rate in November 2025 (2025-11-01 00:00:00 <= ts_utc < 2025-12-01 00:00:00)? A transaction counts as declined if its response code is flagged as a decline in the response-code dictionary version that was valid at the transaction's timestamp. Decline rate = declined / all transactions of that model in the month (any status). Answer as a decimal fraction rounded to 4 decimals.
gt_sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(rc.is_decline), 4) AS decline_rate
FROM txn t
JOIN dim_terminal d ON d.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
JOIN dim_terminal_model mo ON mo.model_id = d.model_id
JOIN response_code_dict rc ON rc.code = t.response_code
  AND t.ts_utc >= rc.valid_from AND (rc.valid_to IS NULL OR t.ts_utc < rc.valid_to)
WHERE mo.model_name = 'Lane 3000X'
  AND t.ts_utc >= '2025-11-01 00:00:00' AND t.ts_utc < '2025-12-01 00:00:00'
rationale: Scheme version 3 (valid from 2025-10-01, present only in the migrated DB) re-maps Z1 and 91 from timeout to decline; using the remembered version 2 under-counts declines in November.

text: Incident INC-2025-0021 is linked to service events through correlation ids. Find the earliest ERROR-level service event linked to this incident. Which config change on the incident's component was the most recent one made strictly before that event? Answer with its change_id (integer).
gt_sql:
WITH inc AS (SELECT incident_id, component_id FROM incident WHERE code = 'INC-2025-0021'),
ev AS (
  SELECT ts_utc, level, correlation_id FROM service_event_h1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ts_utc, level, correlation_id FROM service_event_h2),
first_err AS (
  SELECT MIN(e.ts_utc) AS ts
  FROM ev e
  JOIN incident_link l ON l.correlation_id = e.correlation_id
  JOIN inc ON inc.incident_id = l.incident_id
  WHERE e.level = 'ERROR')
SELECT cc.change_id
FROM config_change cc JOIN inc ON inc.component_id = cc.component_id
WHERE cc.changed_at < (SELECT ts FROM first_err)
ORDER BY cc.changed_at DESC LIMIT 1
rationale: The first linked ERROR is 12 minutes before opened_at; r.svensson's jvm.heap_mb change 40 minutes before opening precedes it, while j.mueller's mitigation change 4 minutes before opening does not.

text: For every settlement, recompute the settled EUR amount in cents as ROUND(A * R * 100), where A is the transaction amount in major units of its currency and R is the official daily FX rate (EUR per unit of that currency) for the calendar date of settled_at (UTC); then take the absolute difference between this value and settled_eur_minor. Which ISO-8601 week (by settled_at) has the largest sum of these absolute differences? Answer in the format YYYY-Www.
gt_sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y', date(s.settled_at, '-' || ((strftime('%w', s.settled_at) + 6) % 7) || ' days', '+3 days')) || '-W' || printf('%02d', (strftime('%j', date(s.settled_at, '-' || ((strftime('%w', s.settled_at) + 6) % 7) || ' days', '+3 days')) - 1) / 7 + 1) AS iso_week
FROM settlement s
JOIN txn t ON t.txn_id = s.txn_id
JOIN dim_currency c ON c.currency_id = t.currency_id
JOIN fx_rate_daily f ON f.currency_id = t.currency_id AND f.rate_date = substr(s.settled_at, 1, 10)
GROUP BY iso_week
ORDER BY SUM(ABS(s.settled_eur_minor - ROUND(t.amount_minor / power(10, c.exponent) * f.eur_per_unit * 100))) DESC
LIMIT 1
rationale: Outside the stale-cache window the recomputation matches exactly; six of the seven stale settlement batches (2025-05-13..18) fall into ISO week 2025-W20.

text: How many distinct terminals were linked to a merchant of merchant group 'Borealis Retail AG' or any of its sub-groups at some moment during May 2025, i.e. the terminal-merchant link interval overlaps [2025-05-01 00:00:00, 2025-06-01 00:00:00)? Answer with an integer.
gt_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE grp(group_id) AS (
  SELECT group_id FROM dim_merchant_group WHERE name = 'Borealis Retail AG'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT g.group_id FROM dim_merchant_group g JOIN grp ON g.parent_group_id = grp.group_id
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT tl.terminal_id) AS n_terminals
FROM terminal_merchant_link tl
JOIN dim_merchant m ON m.merchant_id = tl.merchant_id
JOIN grp ON grp.group_id = m.merchant_group_id
WHERE tl.start_ts < '2025-06-01 00:00:00'
  AND (tl.end_ts IS NULL OR tl.end_ts > '2025-05-01 00:00:00')
rationale: The 44 ex-Aurora coffee terminals were linked to Borealis merchants only from 2025-06-16, so they must not be counted for May; the current-link view includes them.
